methodologyNotes: Roster covers eight high-search CPU coolers spanning AIO liquid and air categories: Arctic Liquid Freezer III 360, NZXT Kraken Elite 360 RGB (2024), Corsair iCUE H150i Elite Capellix XT, Noctua NH-D15 G2, Deepcool LS720, Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE, be quiet! Dark Rock Pro 5, and Lian Li Galahad II Trinity Performance 360. Sources consulted include manufacturer product pages (arctic.de, noctua.at, bequiet.com, deepcool.com, lian-li.com, thermalright.com, corsair.com, nzxt.com), retailer listings (Newegg, Amazon, Micro Center, Best Buy), and independent reviews (GamersNexus, Tom's Hardware, TechPowerUp, KitGuru). Specs strings carry units where applicable (e.g. "360 mm", "168 mm"); booleans indicate yes/no features; noise_dba_max is the manufacturer-rated or reviewer-measured peak dB(A) at 100% fan speed; tdp_rating_w is the manufacturer-stated maximum dissipation where published, otherwise null. Adversarial re-verification 2026-06-15: corrected Corsair socket list (removed LGA1851, which the XT does not support per the official Corsair page and Amazon listing) and nulled Thermalright PA120 SE tdp_rating_w (Thermalright does not publish a hard numeric TDP ceiling; spec pages state only "TDP exceeding 200 W" — a null beats an unsourced 265 W). accessedAt 2026-06-15.

products.name: Arctic Liquid Freezer III 360

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1700, LGA1851, AMD AM4, AM5 (LGA1200/115x via optional kit)

products.provenance: Release date October 18, 2023 confirmed via GamersNexus review. Launch MSRP $130 for black variant confirmed by multiple sources (A-RGB SKU $150). Noise at 100% fan speed ~40 dBA from GamersNexus testing (20-inch, non-chamber method). Official Arctic page confirms black non-RGB variant, 360 mm radiator, three P12 fans plus a 60 mm VRM fan, LGA1700/LGA1851 + AM4/AM5 native (LGA1200/115x via optional kit). Arctic does not publish a TDP ceiling so that field is null.

products.name: NZXT Kraken Elite 360 RGB (2024)
products.priceNote: Current MSRP (black RL-KR36E-B2) as of June 2026; white ~$249.99

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200/115x; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: Released August 2024. Specs and socket support confirmed from official NZXT product page (Intel LGA1851/1700/1200/115X; AMD AM5/AM4). Fan noise 30.00 dBA per fan confirmed on NZXT product page. Three 120mm F360 RGB Core fans on a 401x120x27 mm radiator. Current black-model price $279.99 observed across multiple sources June 2026. NZXT does not publish a TDP ceiling; field left null. Features a 2.72-inch (640x640) IPS LCD.

products.name: Corsair iCUE H150i Elite Capellix XT

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA115x, LGA2011, LGA2066; AMD AM5, AM4, sTRX4/sTR4

products.provenance: Release date February 2, 2023 confirmed via official Corsair press release. Socket support corrected: official Corsair product page and Amazon listing show Intel LGA115X/1200/1700/2011/2066 and AMD AM5/AM4/sTRX4/sTR4 — the draft's inclusion of LGA1851 was wrong (the XT predates LGA1851) and has been removed. Three AF120 RGB Elite fans, 360 mm radiator. Max fan noise 34.1 dBA from Corsair specs (5-34.1 dB range, 550-2100 RPM). Corsair does not publish a TDP ceiling; field left null. Price reflects current typical US street pricing.

products.name: Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE
products.priceNote: Typical US street price; reviewed September 2022 at ~$36

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1151, LGA1155, LGA1156; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: Height 155 mm, two TL-C12C fans, six heat pipes, noise 25.6 dBA, and socket support confirmed via Thermalright product page and spec aggregator. tdp_rating_w corrected from 265 to null: Thermalright does not publish a hard numeric TDP ceiling for the PA120 SE — the spec page states only "designed for CPUs with a TDP exceeding 200 W," and the 265 W figure is an unsourced aggregator estimate, so a null beats a guess. products.name: be quiet! Dark Rock Pro 5

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1150, LGA1151, LGA1155; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: Launch date October 24, 2023 confirmed via PC Perspective and be quiet! press coverage. products.name: Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120 SE
products.priceNote: Typical US street price; PCSpecChart lists current Amazon price $36 (release price $43).

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA115X, LGA1200, LGA1700, LGA1851; AMD AM4, AM5

products.provenance: The official Thermalright product page confirms this is the exact Phantom Spirit 120 SE (Heatsink > Dual Towers > Phantom Spirit line): heatsink L110 x W125 x H154 mm, seven 6 mm heatpipes, C1100 nickel-plated copper base, and TL-C12B V2 120 mm fans rated 1500 RPM / 25.6 dBA, with Intel LGA115X/1200/1700/1851 and AMD AM4/AM5 support. PCSpecChart (corroboration) confirms the same model by name and part number PS120SE, explicitly stating it includes 2 fans, air cooling type, no RGB, 25.6 dBA noise, 110 x 125 x 154 mm dimensions, and a current Amazon price of $36 (release price $43). Thermalright publishes no numeric TDP ceiling (spec text only cites "TDP exceeding 200 W") so tdp_rating_w is null, and no fetched page states a firm release date for this SKU so release and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Corsair iCUE Link Titan 360 RX RGB
products.priceNote: Corsair.com list price $199.99 (SKU CW-9061018-WW, Black). Tom's Hardware review lists MSRP $199 USD; street price ~$144.99 (Newegg) to $149.99 (Amazon) per the Feb 2025 review.

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: The official Corsair product page (SKU CW-9061018-WW, Black) confirms this exact model — iCUE LINK TITAN 360 RX RGB — listing a 360mm radiator (396x120x27mm), three RX120 RGB fans, copper cold plate, socket support "Intel 1851, Intel 1700, AMD AM5, AMD AM4", fan speed 300-2100 RPM, a rated Noise Level of 10-36 dBA, and a current price of $199.99. Tom's Hardware's February 24, 2025 review corroborates the same model name, an MSRP of $199 USD (street ~$144.99-149.99 at Newegg/Amazon), 300-2100 RPM fans, and Intel LGA 1851/1700 + AMD AM5/AM4 compatibility, confirming this is the first-generation RX RGB and not the newer Titan II. Corsair publishes no numeric TDP ceiling — Tom's Hardware's ">265W" figure is a reviewer test result with an i7-14700K rather than a manufacturer rating — so tdp_rating_w is left null.

products.name: Deepcool AK620
products.priceNote: Launch MSRP $69.99 per Tom's Hardware review (published 8 October 2021: "Priced at $69.99", listed Web Price $70). No US MSRP is published on the manufacturer page.

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA2066, LGA2011-v3, LGA2011, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1151, LGA1150, LGA1155; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: The official DeepCool AK620 product page (P/N R-AK620-BKNNMT-G) confirms this is the base AK620: an air cooler with a dense dual-tower fin array, six Ø6mm copper heatpipes, two 120mm FDB PWM fans, 160 mm height (Product Dimensions 129×138×160 mm), maximum heat dissipation power of 260W, Fan Noise ≤28 dB(A), no RGB, and socket support of Intel LGA2066/2011-v3/2011/1700/1200/1151/1150/1155 plus AMD AM5/AM4. Tom's Hardware's 8 October 2021 review of the base AK620 corroborates the model identity, the no-RGB satin-black dual-tower design, the pair of FK120 120mm PWM fans (rated to 1850 RPM), and states the launch price of $69.99. Release year 2021 is confirmed by the manufacturer URL (/2021/) and the review's publication date; no exact launch month appears verbatim on either fetched page, so releaseDate is kept at year granularity.

products.name: be quiet! Dark Rock Elite
products.priceNote: MSRP $114.90 per TechPowerUp review (dated Feb 1, 2024, "MSRP: $114.90"). Official be quiet! page lists €119.90 RRP (no USD figure). US street price lower: $84.90 on Newegg, ~$100 at Amazon/Newegg per XDA review.

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1150, LGA1151, LGA1155; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: The official be quiet! product page (article BK037) confirms this exact model, the Dark Rock Elite, and every spec verbatim: air cooler, 168 mm height (145 x 136 x 168 mm), two Silent Wings 135 mm PWM fans, 7 copper heat pipes, TDP 280 W, ARGB top cover, and a rated 25.8 dB(A) at 100% (overall noise @ 50/75/100% = 11.0/19.5/25.8) — clearly distinct from the Dark Rock Pro 5 (270 W, no RGB) already in the catalog. Socket support (Intel LGA1851/1700/1200/1150/1151/1155; AMD AM5/AM4) is taken verbatim from the be quiet! page and matches the Newegg BK037 listing (TDP 280W, max 25.8 dB(A), 168 mm height). TechPowerUp's dated review (Feb 1, 2024) states MSRP $114.90 and re-confirms the model (dual-tower, 7 heat pipes, dual 135 mm Silent Wings, 2000 RPM, liquid-metal compatible); the manufacturer page carries no launch date and the actual Oct-2023 launch is not stated verbatim on any fetched page, so releaseDate/release are left null rather than guess a year from retailer listing dates.

products.name: Cooler Master Hyper 212 Halo Black
products.priceNote: GigaParts in-stock US listing $44.99 for the black SKU RR-S4KK-20PA-R1; typical US street price in the low-to-mid $40s.

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1151, LGA1150, LGA1155, LGA1156; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: Official Cooler Master page confirms the exact model — Hyper 212 Halo Black, Product Number RR-S4KK-20PA-R1, Exterior Color Black — with a single 120mm MF120 Halo2 ARGB fan, four heat pipes plus aluminum fins, 124 x 73 x 154 mm (154 mm height), Intel LGA1851/1700/1200/1151/1150/1155/1156 + AMD AM5/AM4, and 27 dBA (Max) noise; it is an Air Cooler and publishes no numeric TDP, so tdp_rating_w is null. GigaParts corroborates the identical RR-S4KK-20PA-R1 spec table and lists the black SKU in stock at $44.99 (US), which is the sourced price. No launch year appears on either gated page (a dated Mar 6 2023 Real Hardware Reviews review indicates a 2023 release, but since that year is absent from the source/corroboration URLs the release field is left null per the verbatim rule).

products.name: Cooler Master MasterLiquid 360 Atmos
products.priceNote: $149.99 USD MSRP per Tom's Hardware review (spec table "MSRP $149.99" and pros "Reasonable $149.99 USD MSRP"). Official Cooler Master page lists no price; The FPS Review pre-launch estimate was $159.

specs.socket_support: Intel LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA1151, LGA1150, LGA1155, LGA1156; AMD AM5, AM4

products.provenance: Model identity confirmed exact: the official Cooler Master specifications table lists product number MLX-D36M-A25PZ-R1, and The FPS Review's dated review (Sep 22, 2023) cites the identical MLX-D36M-A25PZ-R1, confirming this is the standard MasterLiquid 360 Atmos (not the Atmos II or the 240mm variant). Specs are taken verbatim from the official Cooler Master page: Cooler Type "Liquid Cooler", Radiator Size 360, Fan Quantity 3 PCS, ARGB fan LED, Fan Noise Level 27.2 dBA (Max), and Intel LGA1700/1200/1151/1150/1155/1156 + AMD AM5/AM4 sockets. Price $149.99 is the MSRP stated by Tom's Hardware's Sep 21, 2023 review; Cooler Master's own page lists no price, and The FPS Review's pre-launch $159 estimate was superseded by the firm $149.99 MSRP. Cooler Master publishes no manufacturer TDP ceiling (Tom's ~250W is reviewer testing, not a rating), so tdp_rating_w is null; release year 2023 is confirmed by both September 2023 reviews (month left at year granularity since retail availability was still upcoming as of the review dates).
